questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech. He explained that he was reading the newspaper.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

He explained that he was reading the newspaper.

options.text: "I read the newspaper", he explained.
options.html: "I read the newspaper", he explained.

options.text: "I am reading the newspaper", he explained.
options.html: "I am reading the newspaper", he explained.

options.text: "He had been reading the newspaper", he explained.
options.html: "He had been reading the newspaper", he explained.

options.text: "He has been reading the newspaper", he explained.
options.html: "He has been reading the newspaper", he explained.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is "I am reading the newspaper", he explained.

Key Points

  • The given sentence is in 'indirect speech' and we need to convert it to 'direct speech'.
  • When we change an indirect speech to direct speech, we must follow these rules:

​                • The reporting verb 'exclaimed' remains unchanged.

                • The conjunction 'that' is replaced with inverted commas ("...") to show the direct speech.

                • A comma (,) is added after the direct speech part.

                • The first word of the direct speech is in capital letters.

                • "was reading" is in the past continuous form in the indirect speech. This changes to the present continuous tense "am reading" in the direct speech.

                • The pronoun 'he' changes to 'I'.

  • Thus, option 2 is the correct answer.
     

Hence, direct speech is "I am reading the newspaper", he explained.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech. Sachin exclaimed with joy that he had won the champions cup.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

Sachin exclaimed with joy that he had won the champions cup.

options.text: Sachin shouted, "Hurrah I have to win the champions cup!"
options.html: Sachin shouted, "Hurrah I have to win the champions cup!"

options.text: Sachin said, "Hurrah! I won the champions cup"
options.html: Sachin said, "Hurrah! I won the champions cup"

options.text: Sachin said, "Hurrah! I will win the champions cup."
options.html: Sachin said, "Hurrah! I will win the champions cup."

options.text: Sachin shouted, "Hurrah! I win the champions cup!."
options.html: Sachin shouted, "Hurrah! I win the champions cup!."

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Sachin shouted, "Hurrah! I won the champions cup."

Key Points

  •  We use direct speech when we are repeating or quoting the exact words which were spoken.
  • In the case of direct speech, we place the spoken words between double inverted commas (" ").
  • Also, all types of punctuation be it full stop, question mark or exclamation should be within the inverted commas.
  • In exclamatory statements, we need to use the exclamation mark after an interjection(Oh, Ah, Oops)
  • The sentence in the Indirect Speech is in the Past Perfect tense. Thus, the sentence in the Direct Speech should be in the Past Indefinite tense.
  • Hence, the correct answer is: Sachin said "Hurrah! I won the champions cup."

Therefore,the correct answer is option 2.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech. My mother told me not to buy unnecessary things from the fair.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

My mother told me not to buy unnecessary things from the fair.

options.text: My mother said to me, “You should not have bought unnecessary things from the fair.”
options.html: My mother said to me, “You should not have bought unnecessary things from the fair.”

options.text: My mother said to me, “Do not buy unnecessary things from the fair.”
options.html: My mother said to me, “Do not buy unnecessary things from the fair.”

options.text: My mother said to me, “I hope you did not buy unnecessary things from the fair.”
options.html: My mother said to me, “I hope you did not buy unnecessary things from the fair.”

options.html: My mother said to me, “Unnecessary things should not be bought from the fair.”

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'My mother said to me, “Do not buy unnecessary things from the fair.”'.

Key Points   

  • The given sentence is in indirect speech.
  • Indirect speech:- Indirect speech is a speech which tells you what someone said, but does not use the person's actual words.
    • For example:- 'They said you didn't like it', 'I asked her what her plans were', and ' Citizens complained about the smoke'.
  • We have to convert it into direct speech.
  • Direct speech:- The reporting of speech by repeating the actual words of a speaker.
    • For example:- ‘I'm going,’ she said.
  • In order to convert the given indirect speech into a direct speech, we have to follow some of the steps:-
  • The reported verb told of an indirect speech should be converted into said to in a direct speech.
  • Reported speech should be written in inverted commas while converting an indirect speech into a direct speech.
  • Not to buy present in an indirect speech should be converted into do not buy in a direct speech.

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

questions.solution: The correct answer is “Did you go to school on Tuesday?’’ Fiona asked me. When we are converting from indirect to direct speech, we simply reverse the 'past perfect tense' to 'past simple tense'. If the Reported Speech in Direct Narration is introduced by Verbs like “ be”, “have”, “do”, or any other auxiliary Verbs like “can”, “shall”, “will”, the connective “ if ”, “ whether ” is used after the Reporting Verb. 'I had gone' will be changed into 'Did you go'. A question mark will be added in direct speech.

options.html: Mala told, "I can become the class monitor if I try hard enough."

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Mala said, "I can become the class monitor if I try hard enough."

Key Points 

  • The given sentence is in indirect speech and we need to convert it to direct speech.
  • When we change an indirect speech to direct speech, we use the following rules:- 
    • The reporting verb 'said' remains unchanged. 
    • The conjunction 'that' is replaced with inverted commas ("...") to show the direct speech. 
    • A comma (,) is added before the direct speech part. 
    • The first word of the direct speech is in capital letters.
    • The pronoun she in the indirect speech changes to 'I' in the direct speech.
    • The modal verb 'could' changes to 'can'.
    • The simple past tense 'tried' changes to the simple present tense 'try' in the direct speech. 
    • Thus, option 2 is the correct answer.
       

Correct Answer - Mala said, "I can become the class monitor if I try hard enough."

Additional Information  

  • The following table will let us know how tense changes between direct and indirect speech - 

Rules

Direct Speech

Indirect Speech

Simple Present Changes To Simple Past

"I always drink tea", she said

She said that she always drank tea.

Present Continuous Changes To Past Continuous

"I am reading a book", he explained.

He explained that he was reading a book.

Present Perfect Changes To Past Perfect

She said, "He has finished his work"

She said that he had finished his work.

Simple Past Changes To Past Perfect

"Bill arrived on Saturday", he said.

He said that Bill had arrived on Saturday.

Past Continuous Changes To Past Perfect Continuous

"We were living in Paris", they told me.

They told me that they had been living in Paris.

Future Changes To Present Conditional

"I will be in Geneva on Monday", he said

He said that he would be in Geneva on Monday.

Future Continuous Changes To Conditional Continuous

She said, "I'll be using the car next Friday."

She said that she would be using the car next Friday.

Note - The past perfect and past perfect continuous tenses do not change.
